patch_description:
Crossover of the two candidate ansätze that both use an even/odd-split RY
local layer followed by heterogeneous entanglers and a shared final RZ
phase layer. The high-scoring variant (0.52) used 5 distinct parameters:
independent "ry_even"/"ry_odd" rotations, a nearest-neighbor ZZ ring
("zz_ring"), a long-range antipodal CRZ layer ("crz_long"), and a shared
final RZ ("rz_all"). The lower-scoring variant (0.38) instead used a
second same-topology ring with a different gate type (XX after ZZ) which
added depth (54 vs 33) without adding useful information, hurting
generalization despite the same parameter count.

This crossover keeps every structural element that was empirically
associated with the high score (even/odd RY split, ring/antipodal
heterogeneous entangling, final phase layer) but pushes further on the
"fewer distinct params always helps" principle: the ring (IsingZZ) and the
antipodal long-range coupling (CRZ) are tied to the SAME shared parameter
name ("ent") instead of two separate names. Because IsingZZ and CRZ are
generated by different operators (symmetric two-qubit ZZ coupling vs.
control-asymmetric RZ), sharing one scalar between them still yields two
functionally distinct entangling actions -- similar to weight sharing
across heterogeneous layers -- while cutting the circuit's trainable
parameter count from 5 to 4 (6 total with gain/bias). This keeps the depth
and gate count identical to the best-performing variant (28 gates/block,
84 total, depth 33), avoiding the depth blow-up that hurt the other
candidate, while further reducing parameter count for better few-shot
generalization and a smaller train/validation gap.
